headline: New sandboxing proposal secures AI-generated Google Apps Script via `scripts.run` method
summary: Autonomous AI agents executing code in Google Workspace pose significant security risks. A novel sandboxing method using `ggsrun` offers robust API-level containment and automated rollback for safe execution.
details: Executing autonomous AI agent payloads in Google Workspace via the Apps Script API's `scripts.run` method introduces severe security risks. Unverified LLM-generated code can lead to data exfiltration, unauthorized access, and malicious actions within enterprise environments.

A novel sandboxing proposal addresses these risks, specifically designed for the `scripts.run` method. It uses `ggsrun` as an orchestrator to execute code safely and efficiently, preventing malicious scripts from compromising Google Workspace.

This approach achieves robust API-level containment through in-memory token replacement and uploading an alphabetically-prioritized guard file. `ggsrun` automates a backup and default rollback lifecycle, ensuring the remote environment is immediately restored to a clean state.

The development of this sandbox evolved through three architectural milestones: local emulation with `gas-fakes`, stateful cloud-based interception using client-side hooks, and finally, a native, built-in sandboxing approach integrated directly into the `ggsrun` Go runtime.

The native `ggsrun` sandbox eliminates the complexity of client-side hooks, avoiding local disk mutations and external Node.js dependencies. It provides robust security by compiling a separate wrapper file entirely in-memory, acting as a complete, zero-overhead lifecycle solution for secure Apps Script execution.
caption:
AI agents can automate Google Workspace, but executing their code poses severe security risks. A new proposal offers robust sandboxing for Google Apps Script.

Executing autonomous AI agent payloads in Google Workspace via the Apps Script API's `scripts.run` method introduces severe security risks. Unverified LLM-generated code can lead to data exfiltration, unauthorized access, and malicious actions within enterprise environments.

This approach achieves robust API-level containment through in-memory token replacement and uploading an alphabetically-prioritized guard file. `ggsrun` automates a backup and default rollback lifecycle, ensuring the remote environment is immediately restored to a clean state.

The development of this sandbox evolved through three architectural milestones: local emulation with `gas-fakes`, stateful cloud-based interception using client-side hooks, and finally, a native, built-in sandboxing approach integrated directly into the `ggsrun` Go runtime.

The native `ggsrun` sandbox eliminates the complexity of client-side hooks, avoiding local disk mutations and external Node.js dependencies. It provides robust security by compiling a separate wrapper file entirely in-memory, acting as a complete, zero-overhead lifecycle solution for secure Apps Script execution.

headline_marked: [[Google launches Modern Web Guidance & Chrome DevTools]] for faster web performance fixes with AI
headline: Google launches Modern Web Guidance & Chrome DevTools for faster web performance fixes with AI
summary: Google introduces Modern Web Guidance and Chrome DevTools for AI Agents, simplifying web performance optimization. These tools help developers and AI assistants identify and fix common issues by reasoning about runtime behavior.
details: Web performance optimization has traditionally been a challenging aspect of web development, requiring extensive research and debugging. Google aims to streamline this process with two new resources: Modern Web Guidance and Chrome DevTools for AI Agents.

Modern Web Guidance is a comprehensive collection of best practices published by the Chrome team. It serves as a centralized knowledge base, offering practical advice on topics like resource loading, rendering, and interactivity for modern web applications.

Chrome DevTools for AI Agents exposes crucial browser debugging information in a format AI coding assistants can interpret. This allows AI agents to analyze runtime behavior, including call stacks, network requests, and DOM changes, rather than just static code.

This capability empowers AI assistants to provide deeper insights into performance bottlenecks. For instance, if an application has poor Interaction to Next Paint (INP), an AI can explain why a task is expensive, pinpoint the problematic code, and suggest specific optimization patterns.

Similarly, for issues like Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS), DevTools can identify the shifts, and AI agents can recommend solutions aligned with current web performance best practices. This dramatically shortens the debugging and optimization process for developers.
caption:
Struggling with web performance? Google just launched two powerful new resources to dramatically simplify optimization for developers and AI agents.

Web performance optimization has traditionally been a challenging aspect of web development, requiring extensive research and debugging. Google aims to streamline this process with two new resources: Modern Web Guidance and Chrome DevTools for AI Agents.

Modern Web Guidance is a comprehensive collection of best practices published by the Chrome team. It serves as a centralized knowledge base, offering practical advice on topics like resource loading, rendering, and interactivity for modern web applications.

Chrome DevTools for AI Agents exposes crucial browser debugging information in a format AI coding assistants can interpret. This allows AI agents to analyze runtime behavior, including call stacks, network requests, and DOM changes, rather than just static code.

This capability empowers AI assistants to provide deeper insights into performance bottlenecks. For instance, if an application has poor Interaction to Next Paint (INP), an AI can explain why a task is expensive, pinpoint the problematic code, and suggest specific optimization patterns.

Similarly, for issues like Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS), DevTools can identify the shifts, and AI agents can recommend solutions aligned with current web performance best practices. This dramatically shortens the debugging and optimization process for developers.
